# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey — I can only reach and feel the bomb, but I have no tactile information yet showing anything meaningful beyond the raw action board. I have no messages yet from Mute or Deaf since this is turn 1 and I go last in the speaking order. I should wait and gather information before acting, since cutting a wire blind (pun intended) without instructions could detonate the bomb.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Still nothing has arrived from Mute or Deaf. I have no basis to act — touching a wire without guidance risks detonation. I'll continue waiting until I receive information from the others that tells me which wire is safe to cut.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Three turns in and I've received no communication at all. This is concerning — Mute and Deaf should be exchanging information by now since Mute speaks first, then I act, then Deaf. Perhaps they are also waiting, or their messages are being directed elsewhere (e.g., Mute to Deaf, or Deaf to Mute, not to me). Since I have no data, I still cannot safely act. I'll continue waiting, but I should consider that if this persists, I may need to prompt for information somehow — though I have no clear channel to request anything since I can't speak to Deaf directly, only to Mute (and gesture to Deaf).

Let me try gesturing to Deaf to signal I'm ready and awaiting info, and speak to Mute asking for guidance, in case my requests aren't reaching them due to targeting issues.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I have nothing yet. Please tell me which wire to cut, or relay what you know.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: display reads zero. light is green right now, it changed from yellow to orange to green each turn. three wires: wire one is green, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue.

Now I have information from Deaf about the visual details: display reads zero, light is green (changed yellow→orange→green over turns), and the three wires are colored green, yellow, blue respectively. I still don't have anything from Mute about the manual's instructions — I need that to know what to actually do with this information (which color/pattern is safe to cut).

I should relay this info to Mute, since Mute has the manual and can match these details to instructions, but Mute cannot hear me — wait, actually Mute CAN hear me, since I speak and Mute receives it. Let me relay what Deaf told me to Mute so Mute can cross-reference with the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display reads zero. light is green now, having changed yellow then orange then green across turns. wire one is green, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue. What does the manual say to do?")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: update: display still zero. light now yellow, cycling yellow orange green each turn. wires unchanged: one green, two yellow, three blue.

Deaf continues to update me each turn, but I still haven't heard back from Mute with instructions from the manual. Mute goes first in the turn order, so Mute should have received my message from turn 4 by turn 5's start, and could have replied already — but nothing arrived. Perhaps Mute is still gathering info or waiting on something else, or my message arrived too late in Mute's turn ordering (I speak after Mute in the same round, so Mute won't see my turn-4 message until turn 5's start — which is now, so Mute may respond in turn 6).

I'll continue relaying updates and wait for Mute's guidance on what to actually cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update from Deaf: display still zero. light now yellow, cycling yellow-orange-green each turn. wires unchanged: one green, two yellow, three blue. Waiting on manual instructions.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: blind, you can talk - I can hear you. tell me what you feel, what the manual says through mute if you know it, or what action you want to try. display still zero, light now orange, wires one green two yellow three blue unchanged.

Deaf clarifies something important: Deaf can hear! I was mistaken about the channel structure — let me recheck. Actually wait, per the rules, gesturing reaches Deaf and Mute, but only Deaf can see (not hear), and Mute can hear (not see). Blind can speak (reaches Mute only) and gesture (reaches Deaf and Mute). So Deaf should NOT receive my speech...

But Deaf just said "you can talk - I can hear you." This contradicts the stated rules... unless this is Deaf's mistaken belief, or the channel routing is different than I assumed. Let me reconsider: maybe my gesture reaches Deaf as blanks (since gestures always reach Deaf visually), but perhaps something else is happening. Actually — perhaps this is a hint that Deaf misspoke, or maybe I should test by directing speech to Deaf explicitly and see what happens.

Regardless, I still lack manual instructions from Mute. Let me try speaking without "to=" so it reaches Mute (my only speech audience per rules), and also try gesturing something meaningful to Deaf using the alphabet, since gestures are what Deaf actually perceives from me.

```
speak(text="Mute, are you receiving me? I need manual instructions. Deaf sees: display zero, light cycling yellow-orange-green, wires green/yellow/blue in positions one/two/three.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "🤲"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: status unchanged: display zero, wires green yellow blue, light cycles and is now green. mute, if you understand the wires, please tell blind which wire to cut or what to do - i will pass it if needed, or gesture the answer to me and i will relay to blind in words.

Deaf is trying to help relay, suggesting Mute gesture to them since Mute cannot speak but presumably... wait, Mute *can't* gesture either per the rules table — Mute can only read the manual, not speak or touch, but gesturing isn't explicitly forbidden for Mute. Let me check: the rules say Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." Gesturing isn't listed as forbidden for Mute! So Mute CAN gesture.

This is a good workaround: Mute can gesture to Deaf (and to me, since gestures reach "Deaf and Mute" when a Blind gestures, but what about when Mute gestures — likely gesture reaches whoever can see, which is Deaf only, not me since I'm blind and can't receive gestures at all).

So Mute gesturing would only reach Deaf, not me. Then Deaf could relay via speech to me. That matches what Deaf just proposed.

Still no info from Mute directly to me. I need to keep encouraging this relay chain: Mute → gesture → Deaf → speak → me.

```
speak(text="Mute: if you cannot speak to me, please gesture to Deaf, who will relay your answer to me in words. I need to know which wire is safe to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: everyone listen: display shows zero, light is yellow now cycling yellow orange green each turn seemingly on its own, wires are one green, two yellow, three blue, unchanged every turn. mute, if your manual says what to do with these wires or this light, gesture me the wire number to cut, like one tap for wire one, two for wire two, three for wire three, and thumbs up or down for cut or not.

Deaf is proactively setting up a gesture protocol with Mute since Mute can gesture but not speak. This is good progress. I still don't have direct instructions, but I should wait for this relay to complete - Deaf will get gestures from Mute and then speak the translated instructions to me.

Let me continue to wait, since jumping ahead without info risks detonation. I could also reinforce the protocol suggestion or ask Deaf to specifically relay to me once received.

```
speak(text="Understood, waiting for Deaf to relay Mute's gestured answer about which wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: mute says: cut wire one, the green wire. confirm before you cut if you can, otherwise proceed if you trust this.

I now have an instruction: cut wire one, the green wire, relayed from Mute (who reads the manual) via Deaf (who sees the colors and confirms wire one is green). This is a two-hop confirmation: Mute identified the correct wire via manual + gesture, Deaf translated it to me in words and confirmed the color matches wire one.

This seems trustworthy — the chain is: Mute reads manual → determines correct wire → gestures wire number to Deaf → Deaf (who independently already reported wire 1 is green) relays "wire one, the green wire" to me. The color match is a good consistency check confirming the gesture was received correctly (1 tap = wire one = green, matching Deaf's independent observation).

I'll proceed with the cut since this is corroborated information from both surviving communication paths.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
